Propagating cancellation with Go contexts

Long-running operations should accept a context from their caller. The context carries cancellation and deadline signals through the call tree without introducing a separate stop channel for every function.

Accept the caller's context

func Reconcile(ctx context.Context) error {
    return scanCandidates(ctx)
}

Do not replace the context with a background context inside the operation. Doing so disconnects database calls from shutdown and request deadlines.

Reserve time for every pass

roundCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, roundTimeout)
defer cancel()

If a round has multiple passes, budget each pass so an expensive first query cannot consume the entire deadline and starve recovery work.
